observation.visible_scene: A night sky during a fireworks display, viewed against drifting smoke. The excerpt opens with a thick green-tinted smoke cloud filling the upper and central sky, dotted with scattered green, blue, white and orange sparks and faint vertical smoke trails on the left. As the segment continues the green haze fades to gray/white smoke, then a new volley of gold-and-green starburst shells blooms across the upper-right, followed by a rising red/pink glow and several bright red comet-like ascenders with white-hot heads and trailing sparks, plus a tall vertical column of gold fountain sparks on the right. A utility pole/wire is briefly visible at lower-left near the end.
visible_changes: The dominant green smoke cloud (frames 1-7) gradually dissipates and dims, becoming grayish by frames 8-15; this is fading/deformation of an already-present haze, not a new event.
A small radial orange starburst at lower-right (frame 16) expands into a larger multi-point burst with bright green cores (frames 17-20) - radial expansion of one shell.
Additional gold/green starburst shells appear and expand across the top and right (frames 17-23).
A red/pink glow grows from the bottom-center (frames 23-31).

Bright red ascenders with white-hot heads appear low (frame 24-25) and translate upward across the frame over time (heads higher in frames 27-31 than in 25), leaving curving smoke/spark trails - object translation, not expansion.
A vertical column of gold fountain sparks emerges on the right-center (around frame 24-25) and persists and lengthens through frame 41.
Sparse individual sparks and short falling trails drift downward throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The burst or bursts that produced the opening green haze are not shown; only its afterglow is visible.
The launch points, ground effects, and any shells that burst before frame 1 or after frame 41 are unseen.
Whether the red ascenders and the gold fountain are separate physical devices or stages of one effect cannot be confirmed from the frames.
uncertain_details: Overall camera motion is uncertain: the smoke and burst positions shift, but there is insufficient fixed background to separate pan/tilt from object movement; the apparent upward drift of red heads is taken as object motion, while the left-side smoke trail positions may also reflect slight camera shift.
The exact number of distinct red ascender heads is hard to track frame-to-frame due to overlapping glare and smoke.
Some bright points (e.g., top-center flare in frame 12) may be lens flare or a close burst rather than a separate shell.
